children.text: vṛddhiśabdaḥ saṃjñātvena vidhīyate pratyekam ādaicāṃ varṇānāṃ sāmānyena tadbhāvitānām atadbhāvitānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: The word <s>vṛddhi</s> is prescribed as a technical designation, individually for the vowels ā, ai, and au, in general both for those produced by that process and for those not produced by it.

children.text: taparakaraṇam aijartham tād api paraḥ taparaḥ iti khaṭvaiḍakādiṣu trimātracaturmātraprasaṅganivṛttaye
children.translated_text: The use of t as a marker is for the sake of ai and au; for even after that, t-marked means having t after it, and this prevents the unwanted occurrence of three- and four-mora lengths in forms such as khaṭvaiḍaka.
<s>Āśvalāyana</s>.
<s>Aitikāyana</s>.
<s>Aupagava</s>.
<s>Aupamanyava</s>.
<s>Śālīya</s>.
<s>Mālīya</s>.
Places where <s>vṛddhi</s> is applied are rules such as “there is vṛddhi before sic in the parasmaipada,” and so on.

children.text: guṇaśabdaḥ saṃjñātvena vidhīyate pratyekam adeṅāṃ varṇānāṃ sāmānyena tadbhāvitānām atadbhāvitānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: The word <s>guṇa</s> is prescribed as a technical designation, individually for the vowels a, e, and o, in general both for those produced by that process and for those not produced by it.
Here, however, the use of t as a marker serves all purposes.
taritā.
cetā.
stotā.
jayanti.
ahaṃ pace.
Places where <s>guṇa</s> is applied are rules such as “there is guṇa of mid,” and so on.
This is a paribhāṣā, an interpretive rule, intended to restrict the substitute-place.
Where an unrestricted application would arise, a restriction is prescribed.

children.text: vṛddhiguṇau svasaṃjñayā śiṣyamāṇau ikaḥ eva sthāne veditavyau
children.translated_text: The vṛddhi and guṇa that are taught by their own technical names should be understood to occur only in place of an ik vowel.
He will state: “there is guṇa of the stem before sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka affixes.”
That should be understood to occur only in place of an ik vowel.
nayati.
bhavati.
And vṛddhi also occurs in akārṣīt.
ahārṣīt.
acaiṣīt.
anaiṣīt.
alāvīt.
astāvīt.

children.text: guṇavṛddhī svasaṃjñayā vidhīyete tatra ikaḥ iti etadupasthitaṃ draṣṭavyam
children.translated_text: Since guṇa and vṛddhi are prescribed by their own technical names, in that context the expression “of ik” should be regarded as supplied.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtaṃ bhavati dvitīyayā ṣaṣṭhī prādurbhāvyate
children.translated_text: What is accomplished? By means of the second case ending, the sixth case relation is brought about.
In the cases of mid, mṛj, roots ending in pug, roots with a light penultimate, and the roots chid, ṛś, kṣip, and kṣudra, the ik vowel is specified by the stem.
For the guṇa operations beginning with those before jus and sārvadhātuka affixes, the stem containing ik is specified.
medyate.
abibhayuḥ.

children.text: ikaḥ iti kim āt sandhyakṣaravyañjanānāṃ mā bhūt
children.translated_text: Why say “of ik”? So that it may not apply to ā, to sandhi vowels, or to consonants.
yānam.
glāyati.
umbhitā.
The renewed mention of guṇa and vṛddhi is for the sake of restriction when they are prescribed by their own technical names.

children.text: iha mā bhūt dyauḥ panthāḥ saḥ imam iti ||
children.translated_text: So that it should not apply here: dyauḥ, panthāḥ, saḥ imam.

children.text: dhātvekadeśo dhātuḥ tasya lopo yasmin ārdhadhātuke tad ārdhadhātukaṃ dhātulopaṃ tatra ye guṇavṛddhī prāpnutaḥ te na bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: A part of a root is a root; an ārdhadhātuka affix in which there is elision of that root is called dhātulopa. In that case, the guṇa and vṛddhi that would be obtained do not occur.
loluvaḥ.
popuvaḥ.
marīmṛjaḥ.

children.text: lolūyādibhyo yaṅantebhyaḥ pacādyaci vihite yaṅo 'ci ca iti yaṅo luki kṛte tam eva acam āśritya ye guṇavṛddhī prāpte tayoḥ pratiṣedhaḥ
children.translated_text: When the pacādi affix ac is prescribed after yaṅanta forms such as lolūya, and when the yaṅ is elided by “yaṅ before ac,” the prohibition is of the guṇa and vṛddhi that would be obtained with reference to that very vowel ac.
Why is “root” mentioned? In lūñ, lavitā.
reḍasi.
parṇaṃ na veḥ.
So that it should not apply when an anubandha or an affix is elided.
In the case of the root riṣ in the sense of hiṃsā, the example for elision of the affix vic is reṭ.

children.text: ārdhadhātuke iti kim tridhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti iti
children.translated_text: Why say “before an ārdhadhātuka”? Consider: “tridhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti.”
So that it should not apply before a sārvadhātuka affix.
“Of ik” is still to be supplied: abhāji rāgaḥ.
Why rely on a bahuvrīhi compound? In knopayati and preddham.
This is a locative of occasion or cause.

children.text: kṅinnimitte ye guṇavṛddhī prāpnutaḥ te na bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The guṇa and vṛddhi that would occur when a kṅit affix is the cause do not occur.
citaḥ, citavān.
stutaḥ, stutavān.
bhinnaḥ, bhinnavān.
mṛṣṭaḥ, mṛṣṭavān.
And with ṅit affixes: cinutaḥ, cinvanti.
mṛṣṭaḥ, mṛjanti.
Here the letter g, too, is indicated after it has become c by the rule of cartva.
After glājistha there is also ksnu: jiṣṇuḥ.
bhūṣṇuḥ.
Only “of ik” is meant.
<s>Laigavāyana</s> desires.

children.text: mṛjer ajādau saṃkrame vibhāṣā vṛddhir iṣyate
children.translated_text: In the transition of mṛj before an affix beginning with a vowel, optional vṛddhi is desired.
“Transition” means the domain in which guṇa and vṛddhi are prohibited.
parimṛjanti, parimārjanti.
parimṛjantu, parimārjantu.
Here the guṇa of a light penultimate is also prohibited.

children.text: acinavam asunavam ity ādau lakārasya saty api ṅittve yāsuṭo ṅidvacanaṃ jñāpakam ṅiti yat kāryaṃ tallakāre ṅiti na bhavati iti ||
children.translated_text: In forms such as acinavam and asunavam, although the lakāra is ṅit, the statement that yāsuṭ is ṅit is an indicatory sign that the operation which applies when an affix is ṅit does not apply merely because the lakāra is ṅit.

children.text: dīdhīvevyoḥ iṭaś ca ye guṇavṛddhī prāpnutaḥ te na bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The guṇa and vṛddhi that would be obtained for dīdhī and vevī and for iṭ do not occur.
ādīdhyanam, ādīdhyakaḥ.
āvevyanam, āvevyakaḥ.
And for iṭ: kaṇitā śvaḥ.
raṇitā śvaḥ.

children.text: vṛddhir iṭo na sambhavati iti laghūpadhaguṇasyātra pratiṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since vṛddhi is not possible for iṭ, the prohibition here concerns the guṇa of a light penultimate.

children.text: bhinnajātīyair ajbhir avyavahitaḥ śliṣṭoccāritā halaḥ saṃyogasaṃjñā bhavanti
children.translated_text: Consonants that are uninterrupted by vowels of a different class and are pronounced in close conjunction receive the technical designation <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunct cluster).
The aggregate is what receives the designation.
The plural here refers to the class.

children.text: tena dvayor bahūnāṃ ca saṃyogasañjñā siddhā bhavati
children.translated_text: Therefore the designation saṃyoga is established for both two consonants and many consonants.
In agniḥ, the cluster is gn.
In aśvaḥ, the cluster is śv.
In karṇaḥ, the cluster is rṇ.
In indraḥ, candraḥ, and mandraḥ, the clusters are ndr and the like.
In uṣṭraḥ, rāṣṭram, and bhrāṣṭram, the clusters are ṣṭr and the like.

children.text: tilān stry āvapati iti nasatarayāḥ natasatarayā vā
children.translated_text: In tilān stry āvapati, the cluster is nstry, or alternatively ntstry.

children.text: halaḥ iti kim titaucchatram saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ iti lopaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: Why say “consonants”? Otherwise in titaucchatram, elision by “elision of the final of a conjunct” would occur.

children.text: anantarāḥ iti kim pacati panasam skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca iti lopaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: Why say “uninterrupted”? Otherwise in pacati panasam, elision by “of s and k at the beginning or end of a conjunct” would occur.
Places where saṃyoga is applied are rules such as “there is elision of the final of a conjunct,” and so on.

children.text: mukhasahitā nāsikā mukhanāsikā tayā ya uccāryate varṇaḥ so 'nunāsikasañjño bhavati
children.translated_text: The nose together with the mouth is the mouth-and-nose; a sound pronounced by that receives the technical designation <s>anunāsika</s> (nasalized).
The anunāsika of āṅ occurs in Vedic usage.
abhra āṃ apaḥ.
gabhīra āṃ ugraputre.
cana āṃ indraḥ.
Why mention the mouth? Otherwise it would apply only to anusvāra.
Why mention the nose? So that it should not apply to ka, ca, ṭa, ta, and pa.
Places where anunāsika is applied are rules such as “the anunāsika of āṅ in Vedic usage,” and so on.
The word tulya is a synonym of sadṛśa, “similar.”
What exists in the mouth is āsya, the place of articulation such as the palate.
Prayatana is effort: a quality of a sound such as being fully contacted.

children.text: tulya āsye prayatno yasya varṇasya yena varṇena saha sa samānajātīyaṃ prati savarṇasañjño bhavati
children.translated_text: A sound whose effort in the mouth is the same as that of another sound, together with that sound, receives the designation <s>savarṇa</s> (homogeneous), with respect to one of the same class.

children.text: catvāra ābhyantarāḥ prayatnāḥ savarṇasaṃjñāyām āśrīyante spṛṣṭatā īṣatspṛṣṭatā saṃvṛtatā vivṛtatā ca iti
children.translated_text: Four internal efforts are relied upon for the designation <s>savarṇa</s>: complete contact, slight contact, closure, and opening.

children.text: a a a iti trayo 'kārā udāttānudāttasvaritāḥ pratyekaṃ sānunāsikā niranunāsikāś ca hrasvadīrghaplutabhedād aṣṭādaśadhā bhidyante
children.translated_text: The three a-vowels, namely a, a, and a, with acute, grave, and circumflex accents, each nasalized and non-nasalized, are divided eighteenfold by the distinctions of short, long, and prolated.

children.text: tathā ivarṇaḥ tathā uvarṇaḥ tathā ṛvarṇaḥ
children.translated_text: So too the i-class, so too the u-class, and so too the ṛ-class.

children.text: ﾱvarṇasya dīrghā na santi taṃ dvādaśabhedam ācakṣate
children.translated_text: For the ﾱ-class there are no long forms; they call it twelvefold.

children.text: saṃdhyakṣarāṇāṃ hrasvā na santi tāny api dvādaśaprabhedāni
children.translated_text: For the diphthongal vowels there are no short forms; these too have twelve subdivisions.

children.text: antaḥsthā dviprabhedāḥ rephavarjitā yavalāḥ sānunāsikā niranunāsikāś ca
children.translated_text: The semivowels, except for r, namely y, v, and l, have two subdivisions: nasalized and non-nasalized.
For r and the sibilant and aspirate sounds there are no homogeneous counterparts.
A class consonant is homogeneous with a class consonant.
The tip of a stick.
The front of a cot.

children.text: āsyagrahaṇaṃ kim kacaṭatapānāṃ bhinnasthānānāṃ tulyaprayatnānāṃ mā bhūt
children.translated_text: Why is 'mouth' specified? So that the sounds k, c, ṭ, t, and p, which have different places but the same effort, should not be included.

children.text: kiṃ ca syāt tarptā tarptum ity atra jharojhari savarṇe iti pakārasya takāre lopaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: And what would result? In 'tarptā' and 'tarptum', under the rule 'a jhal is elided before a homogeneous jhal', the p would be elided before t.

children.text: prayatnagrahaṇaṃ kim icuyaśānāṃ tulyasthānānāṃ bhinnajātīyānāṃ mā bhūt
children.translated_text: Why is 'effort' specified? So that i, c, y, and ś, which have the same place but are of different classes, should not be included.

children.text: kiṃ ca syāt aruś cyotati ity atra jharojhari savarṇe iti śakārasya cakāre lopaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: And what would result? In 'aruś cyotati', under the rule 'a jhal is elided before a homogeneous jhal', the ś would be elided before c.
It must be stated that ṛ and ṝ have the designation <s>savarṇa</s>.
The form with hotṝ.
The form with hotṛ.

children.text: ubhayoḥ ṛvarṇasya ṝvarṇasya cāntaratamaḥ savarṇo dīrgho nāsti iti ṛkāra eva dīrgho bhavati
children.translated_text: Since there is no closest long homogeneous substitute for either ṛ or ṝ, it is ṛ itself that becomes long.

children.text: savarṇapradeśāḥ akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ ity evamādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Places where <s>savarṇa</s> is applied are rules such as 'a vowel of the a-class becomes long before a homogeneous vowel.'

children.text: īt ūt et ityevamantaṃ dvivacanaṃ śabdarūpaṃ pragṛhyasañjñaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: A dual word-form ending in ī, ū, or e receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.
For example, 'agnī'.
For example, 'vāyū'.
For example, 'māle'.
For example, 'pacete'.

children.text: īd ūd et iti kim vṛkṣāv atra
children.translated_text: Why say 'ending in ī, ū, or e'? To exclude 'vṛkṣāv atra'.
And 'plakṣāv atra'.
Why say 'dual'? To exclude 'kumāry atra'.
And 'kiśory atra'.
The use of t as a marker is for the sake of removing ambiguity.

children.text: pragṛhyapradeśāḥ plutapragṛhyā aci nityam ity evamādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Places where <s>pragṛhya</s> is applied are rules such as 'a prolated pragṛhya before a vowel is always so treated.'
When ī and the others are pragṛhya, an exclusion must be stated for forms such as maṇīva.
'The dear young calves of mine hang like the lips of a camel-jewel.'
Like a married couple.
Like jampatī.
Like heaven and earth.

children.text: adasaḥ sambandhī yo makāras tasmāt pare īdūdetaḥ pragṛhyasañjñā bhavanti
children.translated_text: After the m that belongs to <s>adas</s>, ī, ū, and e receive the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.
For example, 'amī atra'.
For example, 'amī āsate'.
For example, 'amū atra'.
For example, 'amū āsāte'.
There is no example for e.
Why say 'of <s>adas</s>'? To exclude 'śamy atra'.
And 'dāḍimy atra'.
Why say 'after m'? To exclude 'amuke atra'.
The form 'śe' receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.

children.text: kim idaṃ śe iti supām ādeśaś chandasi
children.translated_text: What is this 'śe'? It is a substitute for case endings in Vedic usage.
'Not among you, allies in the prize.'
'Among us, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.'
That is, 'yuṣme'.
That is, 'asme'.
For you, wealth.
For me, wealth.
That is, 'tve'.
That is, 'me'.

children.text: chāndasam etad evaikam udāharaṇam asme indrābṛhaspatī iti
children.translated_text: The only Vedic example here is 'asme indrābṛhaspatī'.
Because it is recited that way there.

children.text: itarat tu laukikam anukaraṇam yuṣme iti asme iti tve iti me iti ||
children.translated_text: The others are ordinary imitative forms: 'yuṣme', 'asme', 'tve', and 'me'.

children.text: ekaśca asāvacca ekāc nipāto ya ekāc āṅvarjitaḥ sa pragṛhyasañjño bhavati
children.translated_text: A particle that consists of one vowel and is not ā receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.
a, go away.
i, look at <s>Indra</s>.
u, stand up.
ā, do you indeed think so?
ā, surely that is so.
Why say 'particle'? To exclude 'cakārātra'.
And 'jahārātra'.

children.text: ekāc iti kim pra agnaye vācam īraya
children.translated_text: Why say 'one-vowel'? To exclude 'pra agnaye vācam īraya'.

children.text: anāṅ iti kim ā udakāntāt odakāntāt
children.translated_text: Why say 'not ā'? To exclude 'ā udakāntāt' and 'odakāntāt'.
In the sense of slightness, in connection with an action, and in the senses of limit and extension,

children.text: etam ātaṃ ṅitaṃ vidyād vākyasmaraṇayor aṅit ||
children.translated_text: one should know this ā as marked with ṅ; in sentence-recollection it is not marked with ṅ.
The word 'particle' continues to govern.
Because of its final au, the rule applies to what ends in that.

children.text: odanto yo nipātaḥ sa pragṛhyasañjño bhavati
children.translated_text: A particle ending in o receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.
For example, 'āho'.
And 'utāho'.
The word 'ot' continues to govern.

children.text: sambuddhinimitto ya okāraḥ sa śākalyasya ācāryasya matena pragṛhyasañjño bhavati itiśabde anārṣe avaidike parataḥ
children.translated_text: An o caused by vocative address receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s> according to the teacher <s>Śākalya</s>, when followed by the word iti in non-ṛṣi, non-Vedic usage.
Thus 'vāyo iti' or 'vāyav iti'.
Thus 'bhāno iti' or 'bhānav iti'.

children.text: saṃbuddhau iti kim gav ity ayamāha
children.translated_text: Why say 'in vocative address'? To exclude 'gav iti ayam āha'.

children.text: atra anukāryānukaraṇayoḥ bhedasya avivakṣitatvāt asatyarthavattve vibhaktirna bhavati
children.translated_text: Here, because the difference between the imitated form and the imitation is not intended, since there is no meaningfulness, there is no case ending.
The mention of <s>Śākalya</s> is for optionality.
Why say 'when followed by iti'? To exclude 'vāyo atra'.

children.text: anārṣe iti kim etā gā brahmabandhav ity abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Why say 'non-ṛṣi'? To exclude 'etā gā brahmabandhav ity abravīt'.
'According to <s>Śākalya</s>, when followed by iti, in non-ṛṣi usage' continues to govern.

children.text: uñaḥ pragṛhyasañjñā bhavati itau śākalyasya ācāryasya matena
children.translated_text: The sound u receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s> before iti, according to the teacher <s>Śākalya</s>.
The word '<s>Śākalya</s>' is for optionality.
Thus 'u iti' and 'v iti'.
'Of u' continues to govern.

children.text: uñaḥ itāvanārṣe ūṃ ity ayam ādeśo bhavati dīrgho 'nunāsikaśca śākalyasya matena pragṛhyasaṃjñakaśca
children.translated_text: For u, before iti in non-ṛṣi usage, according to <s>Śākalya</s>'s opinion, the substitute 'ūṃ' is made, long and nasalized, and it too has the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.

children.text: śākalyasya grahaṇaṃ vibhāṣārtham iha apy anuvartate
children.translated_text: The mention of <s>Śākalya</s>, for optionality, continues here also.

children.text: tena trīṇi rūpāṇi bhavanti u iti v iti ūṃ iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there are three forms: 'u iti', 'v iti', and 'ūṃ iti'.
The governing phrase 'according to <s>Śākalya</s>, before iti, in non-ṛṣi usage' has ceased.

children.text: īdantam ūdantaṃ ca śabdarūpaṃ saptamyarthe vartamānaṃ pragṛhyasañjñaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: A word-form ending in ī or ū, when used in the locative sense, receives the designation <s>pragṛhya</s>.
'Upon this body of mine.'

children.text: māmakyāṃ tanvām iti prāpte māmakyāṃ māmakī iti tanvām tanū iti
children.translated_text: Where 'māmakyāṃ tanvām' would be expected, the forms are 'māmakyāṃ' as 'māmakī' and 'tanvām' as 'tanū'.
'Soma has taken his place upon <s>Gaurī</s>.'

children.text: īdūtau iti kim priyaḥ sūrye priyo agnā bhavāti
children.translated_text: Why say 'ī and ū'? To exclude 'priyaḥ sūrye' and 'priyo agnā bhavāti'.
After the word agni, the locative ending has the substitute ḍā.

children.text: saptamīgrahaṇaṃ kim dhītī matī suṣṭutī dhītyā matyā suṣṭutyā iti prāpte
children.translated_text: Why is the word "seventh case" included? Because otherwise, when forms such as dhītī, matī, and suṣṭutī, or dhītyā, matyā, and suṣṭutyā, would be obtained, confusion would arise.
Why is the word "meaning" included? Consider vāpyaśvaḥ.
It is because of the rule beginning with nadī and the like.
The use of t as an indicatory element is for the sake of removing doubt.
If, when ī and ū are elided, "in the seventh case" alone were intended, then because of the word "meaning" it would apply.
And if that following sound is homogeneous with the preceding one, the non-occurrence of āṭ would follow.

children.text: vacanādyatra dīrghatvaṃ tatra api sarasī yadi
children.translated_text: Where lengthening occurs by express statement, there too, if the word is sarasī,

children.text: jñāpakaṃ syāt tadantatve mā vā pūrvapadasya bhūt ||
children.translated_text: it might be an indication that the ending condition applies; or it may not belong to the prior member of a compound.

children.text: dārūpāś catvāro dhātavaḥ dhārūpau ca dvau dābdaipau varjayitvā ghusañjñakā bhavanti
children.translated_text: The four roots of the form dā and the two of the form dhā, except dāp and daip, receive the designation <s>ghu</s>.
For example, ḍudāñ: praṇidadāti.
dāṇ: praṇidātā.
do: praṇidyati.
deṅ: praṇidayate.
ḍudhāñ: praṇidadhāti.
dheṭ: praṇidhayati vatso mātaram, "the calf causes the mother to place it."

children.text: adāp iti kim dāp lavane dātaṃ barhiḥ
children.translated_text: Why say "excluding dāp"? In dāp in the sense of cutting, one has dātaṃ barhiḥ, "the sacrificial grass has been cut."
For daip in the sense of cleansing: avadātaṃ mukham, "the face has been cleansed."
Places where <s>ghu</s> is used are rules such as ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali, and so on.

children.text: asahāyasya ādyantopadiṣṭāni kāryāṇi na sidhyanti iti ayamatideśa ārabhyate
children.translated_text: Since operations taught with an initial or final element do not succeed for something that has no companion, this extension by analogy is begun.
The suffix vati is used in the sense of the seventh case.

children.text: ādāviva ante iva ekasmin api kāryaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Even in a single element, an operation applies as though it were at the beginning or as though it were at the end.

children.text: yathā kartavyam ity atra pratyayādyudāttatvaṃ bhavati evam aupagavam ity atra api yathā syāt
children.translated_text: Just as in kartavyam the accent belonging to a suffix-initial element occurs, so too it should occur in aupagavam.

children.text: yathā vṛkṣābhyām ity atra ato 'ṅgasya dīrghatvam evam ābhyām ity atra api yathā syāt
children.translated_text: Just as in vṛkṣābhyām the lengthening of a belonging to the stem occurs, so too it should occur in ābhyām.
Why say "in one"?

children.text: sabhāsaṃnayane bhavaḥ sābhāsaṃnayanaḥ ākāram āśritya vṛddhasañjñā na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In sābhāsaṃnayanaḥ, "arising in the bringing together of the assembly," the designation vṛddha is not obtained on the basis of the ā sound.

children.text: tarap tamap ity etau pratyayau ghasañjñau bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The two suffixes tarap and tamap receive the designation <s>gha</s>.
kumāritarā, "more maidenly."
kumaritamā, "most maidenly."
brāhmaṇitarā, "more brahminical."
brāhmaṇitamā, "most brahminical."

children.text: ghapradeśāḥ gharūpakalpacelaḍbruvagotramatahateṣu ṅyo 'nekāco hrasvaḥ ity evamādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Places where <s>gha</s> is used are rules such as gharūpakalpacelaḍbruvagotramatahateṣu ṅyo 'nekāco hrasvaḥ, and so on.

children.text: bahu gaṇa vatu ity ete saṅkhyāsañjñā bhavanti
children.translated_text: The words bahu, gaṇa, and vatu receive the designation <s>saṅkhyā</s> (number-word).
bahukṛtvaḥ, "many times."
bahudhā, "in many ways."
bahukaḥ.
bahuśaḥ, "frequently."
gaṇakṛtvaḥ, "by groups, many times."
gaṇadhā, "in groups."
gaṇakaḥ.
gaṇaśaḥ, "group by group."
tāvatkṛtvaḥ, "so many times."
tāvaddhā, "in so many ways."
tāvatkaḥ.
tāvacchaḥ, "so often."
katikṛtvaḥ, "how many times?"
katidhā, "in how many ways?"
katikaḥ.
katiśaḥ, "in how many instances?"

children.text: bahugaṇaśabdayor vaipulye saṅghe ca vartamānayor iha grahaṇaṃ nāsti saṅkhyāvācinor eva
children.translated_text: The words bahu and gaṇa, when they denote abundance and a collection, are not included here; only when they express number are they included.
The designation <s>saṅkhyā</s> is prescribed in order to exclude words such as bhūri.

children.text: ardhapūrvapadaśca pūraṇapratyayāntaḥ saṅkhyāsañjño bhavati iti vaktavyaṃ samāsakanvidhyartham
children.translated_text: It should be stated that a word whose prior member is ardha and which ends in a pūraṇa suffix also receives the designation <s>saṅkhyā</s>, for the sake of rules about compounds.
ardhapañcamaśūrpaḥ.

children.text: ardhaṃ pañcamaṃ yeṣām iti bahuvrīhau kṛte ardhapañcamaiḥ śūrpaiḥ krītaḥ
children.translated_text: After forming a bahuvrīhi meaning "those of which the fifth is a half," the sense is "bought with four and a half śūrpas."
This is the compound taught by the rule taddhitārthā.

children.text: tatra diksaṅkhye sañjñāyām ity anuvṛttes tataḥ saṅkhyāpūrvasya dvigusañjñāyāṃ śūrpād añ anyatarasyām iti añ ṭhañ ca
children.translated_text: There, because "direction and number, in a technical name" continues, when the number-preceded expression gets the designation <s>dvigu</s>, the suffixes añ and ṭhañ are added optionally by the rule śūrpād añ anyatarasyām.
By the rule adhyardhapūrvadvigor lugasañjñāyām, luk-elision applies.
Thus, ardhapañcamakaḥ.
Places where <s>saṅkhyā</s> is used are rules such as saṅkhyā vaṃśyena, and so on.
Because the wording is in the feminine, the word saṅkhyā is connected with it.

children.text: ṣakārāntā nakārāntā ca yā saṅkhyā sā ṣaṭsañjñā bhavati
children.translated_text: A number-word ending in ṣ or ending in n receives the designation <s>ṣaṭ</s>.
First, as ending in ṣ: ṣaṭ tiṣṭhanti, "six stand."
ṣaṭ paśya, "see six."
Ending in n: pañca, "five."
sapta, "seven."
nava, "nine."
daśa, "ten."
The mention of the final element is for the sake of what is taught in the grammatical tradition.
Therefore it does not apply here: śatāni, "hundreds," and sahasrāṇi, "thousands."
In aṣṭānām, the augment nuḍ occurs.
Places where <s>ṣaṭ</s> is used are rules such as ṣaḍbhyo luk, and so on.

children.text: ḍatyantā yā saṅkhyā sā ṣaṭsañjñā bhavati
children.translated_text: A number-word ending in ḍati receives the designation <s>ṣaṭ</s>.
kati tiṣṭhanti, "how many stand?"
kati paśya, "see how many."

children.text: ktaś ca ktavatuś ca ktaktavatū pratyayau niṣṭhāsañjñau bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: The suffixes kta and ktavatu receive the designation <s>niṣṭhā</s>.
kṛtaḥ, "done."
kṛtavān, "one who has done."
bhuktaḥ, "eaten."
bhuktavān, "one who has eaten."
The letter k is for operations conditioned by kit.
The letter u is for operations conditioned by ugit.
Places where <s>niṣṭhā</s> is used are rules such as śvīdito niṣṭhāyām, and so on.

children.text: sarvaśabdaḥ ādir yeṣāṃ tānīmāni sarvādīni sarvanāmasaṃjñāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: These words beginning with sarva are called sarvādi words and receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> (pronoun).
sarvaḥ, sarvau, sarve.
sarvasmai.
sarvasmāt.
sarveṣām.
sarvasmin.
sarvakaḥ.
viśvaḥ, viśvau, viśve.
viśvasmai.
viśvasmāt.
viśveṣām.
viśvasmin.
viśvakaḥ.
ubha.
ubhaya.

children.text: ubhaśabdasya sarvanāmatve prayojanam sarvanāmnas tṛtīyā ca iti
children.translated_text: The purpose of giving the word ubha the status of <s>sarvanāman</s> is the rule sarvanāmnas tṛtīyā ca.

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ vasati ubhayoḥ hetvoḥ vasati
children.translated_text: ubhābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ vasati, "he dwells for both reasons," and ubhayoḥ hetvoḥ vasati, "he dwells for both reasons."
ubhaye.
ubhayasmai.
ubhayasmāt.
ubhayeṣām.
ubhayasmin.
ḍatara and ḍatama.
katara, "which of two?" and katama, "which among many?"
katarasmai and katamasmai.
itara, "other."
anya, "other."
anyatara, "either one."
itarasmai.
anyasmai.
anyatarasmai.
The word tva, meaning "other," is recited twice because of a difference in accent.
One is udātta-accented.
The second is anudātta-accented.
Some recite a single form ending in t.

children.text: tva tvat iti dvāv api ca anudāttau iti smaranti
children.translated_text: They remember both tva and tvat as anudātta-accented.
nema, nemasmai.
By the rule to be stated later, there is optionality in the nominative plural ending jas.
Thus, neme or nemāḥ.
sama, samasmai.

children.text: kathaṃ yathāsaṅkhyam anudeśaḥ samānām same deśe yajeta iti
children.translated_text: How is there correspondence in order, as in the injunction "one should sacrifice in the same place"?
The word sama is intended to receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> when it is a synonym of sarva, not everywhere.
sima, simasmai.
pūrva, para, avara, dakṣiṇa, uttara, apara, and adhara receive it when denoting arrangement, but not when used as proper names.
sva receives it except when it denotes a kinsman or property.
antara receives it in the senses of connection with outside and an upper garment.

children.text: tyad tad yad etad idam adas eka dvi yuṣmad
children.translated_text: tyad, tad, yad, etad, idam, adas, eka, dvi, and yuṣmad.
asmad, bhavat, and kim.
This completes the group beginning with sarva.
The expressions denoting pronouns are forms such as 'smai' belonging to the pronoun.
He will state the prohibition, 'not in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>'.

children.text: tasmin nitye pratiṣedhe prāpte vibhāṣeyam ārabhyate
children.translated_text: When that permanent prohibition would apply, this option is begun.
A compound of direction-words is a directional compound.

children.text: digupadiṣṭe samāse bahuvrīhau vibhāṣā sarvādīni sarvanāmasañjñāni bhavanti
children.translated_text: In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound taught under direction-words, the words beginning with sarva optionally receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>.
For uttarapūrvasyai, also uttarapūrvāyai.
For dakṣiṇapūrvasyai, also dakṣiṇapūrvāyai.

children.text: diggrahaṇaṃ kim na bahuvrīhau iti pratiṣedhaṃ vakṣyati tatra na jñāyate kva vibhāṣā kva pratiṣedhaḥ iti
children.translated_text: Why mention direction-words? Because he will state the prohibition 'not in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>'; there it is not known where there is option and where prohibition.

children.text: diggrahaṇe punaḥ kriyamāṇe jñāyate digupadiṣṭasamāse vibhāṣā anyatra pratiṣedhaḥ iti
children.translated_text: But when direction-words are mentioned, it is understood that in a compound taught under direction-words there is option, and elsewhere there is prohibition.

children.text: samāsagrahaṇaṃ kim samāsa eva yo bahuvrīhiḥ tatra vibhāṣā yathā syāt
children.translated_text: Why mention compound? So that the option may apply to a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> which is itself a compound.

children.text: bahuvrīhivad bhāvena yo bahuvrīhiḥ tatra mā bhūt
children.translated_text: It should not apply to something that is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> only by being treated like a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>.
Give to the southern-southern one.

children.text: bahuvrīhau iti kiṃ dvandve vibhāṣā mā bhūt
children.translated_text: Why say 'in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>'? So that the option may not apply in a <s>dvandva</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇottarapūrvāṇām iti dvandve ceti nityaṃ pratiṣedho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For in the <s>dvandva</s> 'of south, north, and east', there is permanent prohibition.

children.text: sarvanāmasañjñāyāṃ tadantavidher abhyupagamād bahuvrīher api sarvādyantasya sañjñā syāt iti pratiṣedha ārabhyate
children.translated_text: Because the rule that a designation extends to what ends in the designated item is accepted for the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>, even a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> ending in a sarva-class word would receive the designation; therefore the prohibition is begun.

children.text: bahuvrīhau samāse sarvādīni sarvanāmasañjñāni na bhavanti
children.translated_text: In a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, the words beginning with sarva do not receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>.
For priyaviśvāya.
For priyobhayāya.
For dvyanyāya.
For tryanyāya.

children.text: iha ca tvatkapitṛkaḥ matkapitṛkaḥ ityakaj na bhavati
children.translated_text: And here, in tvatkapitṛkaḥ and matkapitṛkaḥ, the affix akac does not occur.

children.text: bahuvrīhau iti vartamāne punarbahuvrīhigrahaṇaṃ bhūtapūrvamātre 'pi pratiṣedho yathā syāt vastrāntaravasanāntarāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Although 'in a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>' is already continuing, the repeated mention of <s>bahuvrīhi</s> is so that the prohibition may apply even to what was formerly only a <s>bahuvrīhi</s>, as in vastrāntaravasanāntarāḥ.
In a third-case compound, the words beginning with sarva do not receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>.
For māsapūrvāya.
For saṃvatsarapūrvāya.
For dvyahapūrvāya.
For tryahapūrvāya.

children.text: samāse iti vartamāne punaḥ samāsagrahaṇaṃ tṛtīyāsamāsārthavākye 'pi pratiṣedho yathā syāt
children.translated_text: Although 'in a compound' is continuing, the repeated mention of compound is so that the prohibition may apply even in a sentence having the meaning of a third-case compound.
For māsena pūrvāya.

children.text: pūrvasadṛśasamonārthakalahanipuṇamiśraślakṣṇaiḥ iti tṛtīyāsamāsaṃ pratipadaṃ vakṣyati tasyedaṃ grahaṇam
children.translated_text: He will teach the third-case compound, word by word, in the rule 'with pūrva, sadṛśa, sama, ūna, artha, kalaha, nipuṇa, miśra, and ślakṣṇa'; this mention refers to that.
It does not refer to just any third-case compound.

children.text: kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam iti tvayakā kṛtam mayakā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: But by 'kṛta, frequently, in the sense of agent and instrument', there are tvayakā kṛtam and mayakā kṛtam.

children.text: dvandve ca samāse sarvādīni sarvanāmasañjñāni na bhavanti
children.translated_text: And in a <s>dvandva</s> compound, the words beginning with sarva do not receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>.
Of pūrva and apara.
Of katara and katama.

children.text: pūrveṇa nitye pratiṣedhe prāpte jasi vibhāṣā ārabhyate
children.translated_text: When permanent prohibition would apply by the preceding rule, an option is begun in the case of <s>jas</s>.

children.text: dvandve samāse jasi vibhāṣā sarvādīni sarvanāmasañjñāni na bhavanti
children.translated_text: In a <s>dvandva</s> compound, with <s>jas</s>, the words beginning with sarva optionally do not receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s>.
katarakatame, katarakatamāḥ.

children.text: jasaḥ kāryaṃ prati vibhāṣā akaj hi na bhavati katarakatamakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The option concerns the operation belonging to <s>jas</s>; for akac does not occur: katarakatamakāḥ.
'Option with <s>jas</s>' continues.
'In a <s>dvandva</s>' has ceased to govern.

children.text: prathamacaramatayālpārdhakatipayanema ity ete jasi vibhāṣā sarvanāmasañjñā bhavanti
children.translated_text: The words prathama, carama, taya, alpa, ardha, katipaya, and nema optionally receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> with <s>jas</s>.
prathame, prathamāḥ.
carame, caramāḥ.
dvitaye, dvitayāḥ.
alpe, alpāḥ.
ardhe, ardhāḥ.
katipaye, katipayāḥ.
neme, nemāḥ.
In taya, the affix is tayap.
The remaining ones are nominal stems.

children.text: tatra nema iti sarvādiṣu paṭhyate tasya prāpte vibhāṣā anyeṣām aprāpte
children.translated_text: Among these, nema is recited among the sarva-class words; for it, the option applies when the designation would otherwise obtain, while for the others it applies when it would not otherwise obtain.

children.text: ubhayaśabdasya tayappratyayāntasya gaṇe pāṭhān nityā sarvanāmasañjñā iha api jaskāryaṃ prati vibhāṣā
children.translated_text: Because the word ubhaya ending in the affix tayap is recited in the class, the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> is permanent; yet here too, with respect to the operation of <s>jas</s>, there is option.
The operation proceeds according to applicability, like the crow and the thief.

children.text: pūrva parāvaradakṣiṇottarāparādhara ityeṣāṃ gaṇe pāṭhāt pūrveṇa nityāyāṃ sarvanāmasañjñāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ jasi vibhāṣā ārabhyate
children.translated_text: Because pūrva, para, avara, dakṣiṇa, uttara, apara, and adhara are recited in the class, the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> would be permanent by the preceding rule; therefore the option is begun with <s>jas</s>.

children.text: pūrvādīni vibhāṣā jasi sarvanāmasañjñāni bhavanti vyavasthāyām asaṃjñāyām
children.translated_text: The words beginning with pūrva optionally receive the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> with <s>jas</s>, when there is relative ordering and when they are not proper names.
Relative ordering is the restriction of a boundary in dependence on what the word itself denotes.
pūrve, pūrvāḥ.
pare, parāḥ.
avare, avarāḥ.
dakṣiṇe, dakṣiṇāḥ.
uttare, uttarāḥ.
apare, aparāḥ.
adhare, adharāḥ.

children.text: vyavasthāyām iti kiṃ dakṣiṇā ime gāthakāḥ
children.translated_text: Why say 'when there is relative ordering'? To exclude 'these singers are dakṣiṇāḥ'.
The meaning is 'skilled'.
Why say 'when they are not proper names'? To exclude 'the northern <s>Kurus</s>'.

children.text: satyām eva vyavasthāyām iyaṃ teṣāṃ sañjñā ||
children.translated_text: Even though relative ordering is present, that is their proper name.

children.text: atra api nityā sarvanāmasañjñā prāptā jasi vibhāṣyate
children.translated_text: Here too, the permanent designation <s>sarvanāman</s> would apply, and it is made optional with <s>jas</s>.

children.text: svam ity etacchabdarūpaṃ jasi vibhāṣā sarvanāmasañjñaṃ bhavati na cej jñātidhanayoḥ sañjñārūpeṇa vartate
children.translated_text: This word-form svam optionally receives the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> with <s>jas</s>, provided that it is not used as a name for kin or wealth.
sve putrāḥ, svāḥ putrāḥ.
sve gāvaḥ, svā gāvaḥ.
The meaning is 'one's own'.

children.text: jñātipratiṣedhaḥ iti kim dhūmāyanta iva aśliṣṭāḥ prajvalanti iva saṃhatāḥ
children.translated_text: Why the prohibition concerning kin? As in: 'As if smoking, though not clinging together; as if blazing, though assembled...'

children.text: ulmukāni iva me 'mī svā jñātayo bharatarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: 'These svāḥ of mine, my kinsmen, are like firebrands, O bull of the <s>Bharatas</s>.'

children.text: adhanākhyāyām iti kim prabhūtāḥ svā na dīyante prabhūtāḥ svā na bhujyante
children.translated_text: Why say 'when not denoting wealth'? To exclude: 'abundant svāḥ are not given; abundant svāḥ are not enjoyed.'
The meaning is 'abundant riches'.

children.text: atra api pūrveṇa nityā sarvanāmasañjñā prāptā sā jasi vibhāṣyate
children.translated_text: Here too, by the preceding rule, permanent designation as <s>sarvanāman</s> would apply, and it is made optional with <s>jas</s>.

children.text: antaram ity etacchabdarūpaṃ vibhāṣā jasi sarvanāmasañjñaṃ bhavati bahiryoge upasaṃvyāne ca gamyamāne
children.translated_text: This word-form antaram optionally receives the designation <s>sarvanāman</s> with <s>jas</s>, when exterior connection or an upper garment is understood.
antare gṛhāḥ, antarāḥ gṛhāḥ.
Houses outside the city, such as those of <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, are meant.
In the sense of an upper garment: antare śāṭakāḥ, antarāḥ śāṭakāḥ.
An under-garment is called something to be put on, not something to be used as an outer covering.

children.text: bahiryogopasaṃvyānayoḥ iti kim anayoḥ grāmayor antare tāpasaḥ prativasati
children.translated_text: Why is it said, 'in external conjunction and in under-garment'? Between these two villages an ascetic lives.
In that intervening space there are cold waters.
The word antara denotes a middle region.
And this is a counter-example to the gana-sutra.
It must be stated: 'not after pur'.
He lives in the inner city.

children.text: vibhāṣāprakaraṇe tīyasya vā ṅitsu sarvanāmasañjñā ity upasaṃkhyānam
children.translated_text: In the section on optionality, there is an additional statement that the word tiya optionally has the designation sarvanama when it is marked with n.
For the second; to the second.
For the third; to the third.
The word-forms beginning with svar, and the particles, have the designation avyaya.

children.text: svar antar prātar ete antodāttāḥ paṭhyante
children.translated_text: Svar, antar, and pratar: these are recited with final acute accent.
Punar has initial acute accent.

children.text: sanutar uccais nīcais śanais ṛdhak ārāt ṛte yugapat pṛthak ete 'pi sanutarprabhṛtayo 'ntodāttāḥ paṭhyante
children.translated_text: Sanutar, uccais, nicais, sanais, rdhak, arat, rte, yugapat, and prthak: these too, beginning with sanutar, are recited with final acute accent.

children.text: hyas śvas divā rātrau sāyam ciram manāk īṣat joṣam tūṣṇīm bahis āvis avas adhas samayā nikaṣā svayam mṛṣā naktam nañ hetau addhā iddhā sāmi ete 'pi hyasprabhṛtayo 'ntodāttāḥ paṭhyante
children.translated_text: Hyas, svas, diva, ratrau, sayam, ciram, manak, isat, josam, tusnim, bahis, avis, avas, adhas, samaya, nikasa, svayam, mrsa, naktam, nan, hetau, addha, iddha, and sami: these too, beginning with hyas, are recited with final acute accent.
What ends in vat or vati has the designation avyaya.
Like a brahmana.
Like a kshatriya.

children.text: san sanāt sanat tiras ete ādyudāttāḥ paṭhyante
children.translated_text: San, sanat, sanat, and tiras: these are recited with initial acute accent.
Antarayam has final acute accent.

children.text: antareṇa jyok kam śam sanā sahasā vinā nānā svasti svadhā alam vaṣaṭ anyat asti upāṃśu kṣamā vihāyasā doṣā mudhā mithyā
children.translated_text: Antarena, jyok, kam, sam, sana, sahasa, vina, nana, svasti, svadha, alam, vasat, anyat, asti, upamsu, ksama, vihayasa, dosa, mudha, and mithya.
A krt form ending in ktva, tosun, or kasun, one ending in m, one ending in a diphthongal vowel, and an avyayibhava compound also have the designation avyaya.

children.text: purā mitho mithas prabāhukam āryahalam abhīkṣṇam sākam sārdham samama namas hiruk tasilādiḥ taddhita edhācparyantaḥ śastasī kṛtvasuc suc āsthālau cvyarthāśca am ām pratān praṣān svarādiḥ
children.translated_text: Pura, mitho, mithas, prabahukam, aryahalam, abhiksnam, sakam, sardham, samama, namas, hiruk, the tasil-class, the taddhita class ending with edhac, sastasi, krtvasuc, suc, asthalau, forms in the sense of cvi, am, am, pratan, prasan, and the svaradi class.
Particles will be taught in the rule 'particles before isvara'.

children.text: ca vā ha aha eva evam ityādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Ca, va, ha, aha, eva, evam, and so on.
Occurrences of the word avyaya are such rules as 'after an avyaya, ap and sup'.
The designation avyaya is etymologically meaningful.

children.text: sadṛśaṃ triṣu liṅgeṣu sarvāsu ca vibhaktiṣu
children.translated_text: That which is the same in the three genders and in all the cases,

children.text: vacaneṣu ca sarveṣu yanna vyeti tadavyayam ||
children.translated_text: and in all the numbers, and does not change, is an avyaya.
A word ending in a taddhita suffix, when it does not have all case forms, receives the designation avyaya.
That from which not all case endings arise is called asarvavibhakti, 'not having all case forms'.

children.text: tataḥ yataḥ tatra yatra tadā yadā sarvadā sadā
children.translated_text: Tatah, yatah, tatra, yatra, tada, yada, sarvada, and sada.

children.text: taddhitaḥ iti kim ekaḥ dvau bahavaḥ
children.translated_text: Why say 'taddhita'? To exclude eka, dvau, and bahavah.

children.text: asarvavibhaktiḥ iti kim aupagavaḥ aupagavau aupagavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why say 'not having all case forms'? To exclude aupagavah, aupagavau, and aupagavah.

children.text: kṛd yo makārāntaḥ ejantaś ca tadantaṃ śabdarūpam avyayasañjñaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: A word-form ending in a krt suffix that ends in m, and one ending in a diphthongal vowel, receives the designation avyaya.
He eats after making it tasty.
He eats after making it prepared.
He eats after making it salty.
Those ending in a diphthongal vowel are vakse and rayah.
These two are yours among chariots.
For wisdom, for skill, for life.
And for long seeing the sun.

children.text: vakṣe iti vaceḥ tumarthe sesenase iti sepratyaye kutve ṣatve ca kṛte rūpam
children.translated_text: Vakse is a form from the root vac, with the suffix se in the infinitive sense by the rule sesenase, after gutturalization and retroflexion have been made.

children.text: eṣe iti iṇaḥ sepratyaye guṇe ṣatve ca kṛte rūpam
children.translated_text: Ese is a form from the root in, after the suffix se has been applied and guna and retroflexion have been made.

children.text: jīvase iti jīveḥ ase pratyaye rūpam
children.translated_text: Jivase is a form from the root jiv with the suffix ase.

children.text: dṛśe iti dṛśeḥ kenpratyayo nipātyate dṛśe vikhye ca iti
children.translated_text: Drse is taught as having the affix ken from the root drs by the rule 'for drse and vikhye'.
The mention of 'ending' is for understanding what is taught in the grammatical instruction.

children.text: iha mā bhūt ādhaye cikīrṣave kumbhakārebhyaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: It should not apply here: adhaye, cikirsave, and kumbhakarebhyah.

children.text: ktvā tosun kasun ity evamantaṃ śabdarūpam avyayasañjñaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: A word-form ending in ktva, tosun, or kasun receives the designation avyaya.
Having done.
Having taken away.
For tosun: 'Before sunrise, at daybreak, O Radheya.'
Before the removal of the calves.

children.text: bhāvalakṣaṇe stheṇkṛñvadi iti iṇaḥ kṛñaś ca tosun pratyayaḥ
children.translated_text: In the sense of denoting the action, the tosun suffix is applied after i and kr by the rule concerning stha, in, kr, and vad.
For kasun: kasun is applied after srp and trd.
Before the cruel one creeps apart, O mighty one.
Before he pierces the collarbones.
An avyayibhava compound receives the designation avyaya.
What is the purpose? Elision, accent of mukha, and phonetic treatment.
For elision: 'Near the fire, moths fall'; 'toward the fire'.
For accent of mukha: upagnimukha and pratyagnimukha.

children.text: mukhaṃ svāṅgam ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prāptam nāvyayadikśabda iti pratiṣidhyate
children.translated_text: Since mukha is a bodily limb, final accent on the following member would be expected, but it is prohibited by the rule 'not after an avyaya or a direction-word'.
When that is prohibited, only the original accent of the prior member remains.
For phonetic treatment: upapayahkarah and upapayahkamah.
The treatment of the s that stands in place of visarga is called upacara.

children.text: tatra avyayībhāvasya avyayatve ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇīṣv anavyayasya iti paryudāsaḥ siddho bhavati
children.translated_text: There, when an avyayibhava has the status of an avyaya, the exclusion in 'after a, before kr, kam, kamsa, kumbha, patra, kusa, and karni, when the preceding word is not an avyaya' is established.

children.text: sarvam idaṃ kāṇḍaṃ svarādāv api paṭhyate
children.translated_text: This entire section is also recited under the svaradi class.
The repetition is for indicating non-permanence.
By that, this restriction of the operation is established.

children.text: iha ca purā sūryasyodeto rādheyaḥ purā krūrasya visṛpo virapśin iti na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalarthatṛnām iti ṣaṣṭhīpratiṣedho na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And here, in 'before sunrise, O Radheya' and 'before the cruel one creeps apart, O mighty one', the prohibition of the genitive by 'not for words meaning time, indeclinables, nistha, khalarthas, and trn' does not apply.
This shi has the designation sarvanamasthana.

children.text: kim idaṃ śi iti jaśśasoḥ ṣiḥ iti śiḥ ādeśaḥ
children.translated_text: What is this shi? It is the substitute shi by the rule 'shi in place of jas and sas'.
The pots stand.
Look at the pots.
Curds.
Honeys.
Tins.
Lacs.

children.text: sarvanāmasthānapradeśāḥ sarvanāmasthāne ca asaṃbuddhau ity evamādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Occurrences of sarvanamasthana are such rules as 'in a sarvanamasthana, when not in address'.

children.text: suṭ iti pañca vacanāni sarvanāmasthānasañjñāni bhavanti napuṃsakād anyatra
children.translated_text: The five endings beginning with su, called suṭ, receive the designation <s>sarvanāmasthāna</s> (pronominal-position endings), except after a neuter stem.
In the neuter there is neither an injunction nor a prohibition.

children.text: tena jasaḥ śeḥ sarvanāmasthānasañjñā pūrveṇa bhavaty eva
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>sarvanāmasthāna</s> designation of jas and śi does indeed arise by the preceding rule.
rājā, rājānau, rājānaḥ.
rājānam, rājānau.
Why say suṭ? To exclude: 'see the king's'.
Why say 'of what is non-neuter'? To exclude sāmanī and vemanī.

children.text: na iti pratiṣedhaḥ vā iti vikalpaḥ
children.translated_text: The word na is a prohibition; the word vā is an option.

children.text: tayoḥ pratiṣedhavikalpayoḥ vibhāṣā iti sañjñā bhavati
children.translated_text: For those two, prohibition and option, there is the designation <s>vibhāṣā</s>.
The use of iti is for indicating the meaning.
In places where <s>vibhāṣā</s> is prescribed, prohibition and option present themselves.

children.text: tatra pratiṣedhena samīkṛte viṣaye paścād vikalpaḥ pravartate
children.translated_text: There, after the domain has been made even by the prohibition, the option then operates.
They cause cases of <s>ubhayatravibhāṣā</s>, optionality in both conditions.
With optionality for the root śvi: śuśāva, śiśvāya.
śuśuvatuḥ, śiśviyatuḥ.
Places where <s>vibhāṣā</s> is prescribed are such rules as 'vibhāṣā śveḥ' and so on.
In 'of ac', the genitive is used in the sense of selection.
And this singular is used with reference to the class.

children.text: acāṃ saṃniviṣṭānām antyād acaḥ paro mid bhavati
children.translated_text: Of vowels set in sequence, after the final vowel there is a mit element.
This is an exception to the condition that the substitute is related to the place of replacement and follows the affix.
viruṇaddhi.
muñcati.
payāṃsi.
Places prescribing mit are such rules as 'śnam after rudh and the others'.

children.text: masjer antyāt pūrvaṃ numam icchanty anuṣaṅgasaṃyogādilopārtham
children.translated_text: In the case of masj, they desire a num before the final element, for the sake of elision of the augment and of a conjunct and so on.
magnaḥ.
magnavān.
maṅktā.
maṅktum.
The word eci has ceased to govern.
The word aci continues to govern.

children.text: āṭaḥ paro yo ac aci ca pūrvo ya āṭ tayoḥ pūrvaparayoḥ āḍacoḥ sthāne vṛddhir ekādeśo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After āṭ, the vowel that follows, and before a vowel, the preceding āṭ: in place of those two, the preceding and following āḍ and ac, there is a single substitute vṛddhi.
aikṣiṣṭa.
aikṣata.
aikṣiṣyata.
aubhīt.
ārdhnot.
aubjīt.

children.text: cakāro 'dhikavidhānārthaḥ usi omāṅoś ca iti pararūpabādhanārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The letter c is for prescribing something additional, namely to block the pararūpa substitution in 'usi omāṅoś ca'.
ausrīyat.
auṅkārīyat.

children.text: ā ūḍhā oḍhā tām aicchat auḍhīyat ||
children.translated_text: ā ūḍhā, oḍhā; he desired her; auḍhīyat.
